summary: Stone summit tower on Bear Mountain, Palisades Interstate Park Commission land, built 1931-34; still used as a fire lookout in high fire danger; observation deck open to the public in 2016.

facts.design: Stone observation tower with a 20 by 20 foot lookout cab; stone quarried by hand from the mountain

access.note: Observation deck was open to the public in a 2016 visit report; the park signs the way. Staffed as a fire lookout only during high fire danger.

visit.trail_note: At the summit of Bear Mountain; the Appalachian Trail passes by its base

events.note: Predecessor steel fire tower erected on the summit, about 60 feet, staffed by park rangers; Wikipedia dates this predecessor's construction to 1928
Predecessor steel tower stood until 1930, when the report says it was removed, possibly to make way for the stone tower
Stone tower completed and opened under CCC administration per the attached report; the register dates construction 1931-34
Tower dedicated as the George W. Perkins Memorial Tower; newspaper dated November 1, 1934

notes_for_editor: Height disagrees: register 40 ft, attached report 50 ft, 1934 newspaper 'some sixty feet'; record height_m 19.8 (about 65 ft) matches neither the register nor the report, so facts omit height. Opening: report says completed and open 1933; register says 1931-34. Honoree: register says 'a Chairman'; 1934 newspaper says the first president; Wikipedia names George W. Perkins Sr. Predecessor steel tower: report says 1923 and removal at 1930; Wikipedia's 1928 tower, taken down seven years later to make room for the stone tower, appears to be the same predecessor, so the story reports the disagreement on its date. Footings distance: 500 ft (2016 visit report) vs 300 ft (report). Wikipedia (lead only) claims fire use until 1953 and a 1990 family funding pledge; not verified against a primary source. Do not confuse the stone tower with the 1923 steel tower the report titles 'Lost Fire Tower'. No current-hours source found; the observation deck status comes from a 2016 visit report. County is unconfirmed: the record and the Forest Lookouts header say Orange; a historical marker (hmdb.org m=65286, seen in search only) says Rockland; Wikipedia says the mountain lies partly in each, so the story names no county. Record source 'firelookout.org/lookouts/us/ny/' was not read.
